svg.title: Z80 ROMless SBC: hardware and software architecture
svg.desc: Implementation-based Stage 10 architecture. The Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W is a multicore I/O controller. Core 0 generates the 20 MHz Z80 clock, scope-measured on the project prototype, injects boot instructions, verifies SRAM and handles Z80 I/O traps. Core 1 owns USB initialization, interrupts and endpoints, plus storage, Wi-Fi and WebSocket networking. Core 1 starts before loading and participates in flash lockout during recovery. Fixed console rings, bounded supervisor commands, diagnostics and request/result mailboxes separate the cores. The Z80 alone drives memory addresses and writes SRAM, including during assisted loading. After independent read-back verification and reset, it executes CP/M directly from 64 KiB SRAM.
svg.text: A real Z80 executes CP/M from SRAM. A dual-core Pico 2 W provides boot, clock, virtual I/O and networking.
RP2350 multicore I/O controller | clk_sys = 120 MHz

Direct SRAM bus: Z80 drives A0-A15; D0-D7 bidirectional. Pico never masters memory.
ROMLESS COLD BOOT TO CODE EXECUTION
Core 1 owns USB before loading; storage/network workers remain gated until run
Runtime flash programming: core 1 requests a core-0 BUSREQ#/BUSACK# grant + SDK flash-safe execution; release after commit. No SRAM bus mastering.
I/O cycle: HCT32 asserts WAIT#; core 0 stops PWM, transfers one byte, releases WAIT#, steps to cycle end, isolates data paths and resumes PWM.
Implementation: Stage 10 / core-1 USB migration | Shared Stage 9 main.c. Blue = Z80 I/O and USB queues; teal = networking; orange = clock; purple = SRAM.
20 MHz is the configured nominal Z80 clock, not a claim of combined network timing qualification. Boot failures hold RESET# LOW; trap faults fail closed via reset/watchdog.
